question.text: Which of the following is the correct tax treatment for capital gains arising on redemption of Sovereign Gold Bonds at maturity by an INDIVIDUAL investor?

answer.text: Capital gains are fully exempt from tax
Capital gains are taxed at 12.5% without indexation
Capital gains are taxed at 20% with indexation
Capital gains are taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that redemption of SGBs by an individual investor does not amount to a transfer and no capital gains arise. Investors other than individuals are taxed separately on redemption, so the stem must specify individual investors for the full exemption to apply. The Trap: The 12.5% without indexation rate and slab-rate options reflect treatment on transfer or on non-individual investors, not redemption at maturity by an individual. The 20% with indexation rate is not the prescribed treatment here. Note: Based on NISM Series X-B workbook p.266, which sets out the individual-investor exemption on SGB redemption at maturity.
